AraC-family sarcosine-responsive activator of the sox operon. Confirmed sarcosine-responsive by beta-galactosidase reporter at 1 mM sarcosine and by EMSA, but no numerical ligand Kd is reported in this paper. One web search on 2026-10-06 found none in any later paper either, but that is a failed search rather than proof of absence: not systematic, and no paywalled full texts were read. SouR is the first bacterial regulator shown to respond to sarcosine and induction is specific: glycine betaine, dimethylglycine, glycine and pyruvate all fail to induce the sox operon, so selectivity looks good but is unquantified, so kd_uM is empty and no type-B response can be computed. Activator, not a derepressed repressor.

No numerical Kd in this paper. Two web searches on 2026-10-06 found none elsewhere either, but that is a failed search, not a proof of absence - it was not a systematic review and no paywalled full texts were read. What was checked: the mechanism paper 10.1128/jb.00097-12 characterises PuuR by gel shift and DNase I footprinting only, and no crystal structure of the putrescine-bound effector site surfaced. Gel-shift titration used 0, 10, 50 and 100 mM putrescine, i.e. roughly three orders of magnitude above urinary clinical levels, so even the qualitative working range sits far above the clinical window. Spermidine had little or no effect, so selectivity over spermidine is plausible.
